source.title: (tentatively) Found 600+ Monosemantic Features in a Small LM Using Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: The post text is present, but referenced images and graphs are not included.
record.tranche_reason: It uses sparse-autoencoder features and neuron-activation comparisons, rather than the original vision-neuron method, to examine a selected example the author describes as representing a polysemantic neuron.
record.gate_note: The post reports a selected-feature case study and neuron-count comparisons. It does not report a population estimate of polysemantic neurons. The described ablations of context and feature direction concern the learned feature's activation or logits, not a count of polysemantic neurons.
record.test_reason: The post trains a sparse autoencoder on Pythia-70M layer 2 MLP activations and reports how well its learned features are interpreted. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, nor how common such neurons are. It assumes that neurons are polysemantic and features are in superposition. It says it deliberately chose a feature that 'represents a polysemantic neuron', but gives no neuron-level evidence for that. The neuron counts describe how one SAE feature spreads across neurons, which is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author tentatively claims the SAE learned 600+ interpretable features in Pythia-70M layer 2 mid-MLP, out of an expected 8k–16k. He argues the LaTeX '$' feature is a linear combination of many neurons rather than a single monosemantic neuron. He stresses the work is exploratory and that better metrics and evaluation are needed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse autoencoders trained on Pythia-70M layer_2 activations, feature interpretation, and neuron-basis comparisons rather than the original vision-model feature analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The author notes that conclusions about neuron counts depend on the activation threshold and how the neuron quantiles or feature-vector weights are interpreted.

fits_no_version.finding: A hand-picked interpretable SAE feature (LaTeX '$', #52) in Pythia-70M layer 2 spans an estimated 3 to 80+ neurons depending on threshold. Features from an identity-like dictionary mostly map to 1 neuron.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpretable features in LM MLP layers are distributed across many neurons rather than aligned with single neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features with lower max cosine similarity across dictionaries appear more polysemantic, and many are dead. This rests on a quick qualitative check of about 70 features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemanticity of learned dictionary features (not neurons) tracks how consistently they are learned across dictionaries.

record.problems: The post is exploratory and relies on a selected feature and quick inspection of features. Referenced plots and example images are absent from the supplied text; the author says the neuron-count estimate is unclear and that low-MCS features were mostly not checked.
record.rows_left_out: Feature #52's context-ablation and feature-direction logit-ablation results, activation-range examples, created examples, and MCS/feature counts concern the SAE feature's interpretation or model logits rather than directly measuring individual neurons' responses to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: Share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens, and variation across layers; no neuron-level polysemanticity measured.
No manipulation of feature count versus neuron count. The SAE framing assumes superposition but does not test it.
Initialization, regularization or noise as causes; not studied.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures or regularization.
No re-analysis of canonical polysemantic neurons.
Threshold dependence is noted only for counting the neurons a feature spans, not for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

record.verdict_notes: Exploratory blog post; images are missing from the text. The 'polysemantic neuron' wording is the author's framing, with no neuron-level test behind it. The reader's V2 limits_scope label is removed because no row measures V2.

versions.untested_parts: Vision models and the InceptionV1 examples.
Prevalence across language-model MLP neurons, other models, and layer-to-layer variation; the post studies a selected feature in Pythia-70M layer_2.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity; no pressure manipulation or comparison of feature count to neuron count as a causal test.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Comparisons of activation functions, architectures, or regularization and any performance cost.
Whether the mixed inputs of a neuron share one feature or related job; the post interprets a learned SAE feature, not a canonical mixed neuron with improved tools.
Whether the classification of an individual neuron as polysemantic changes with activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M layer_2 mid-MLP (after the GeLU)
rows.operation_detail: Counted neurons activating above a threshold across the top-10 examples for feature #52.
rows.measure: Number of neurons activating above threshold for all 10 examples
rows.note: This counts neurons active across examples but does not report whether each neuron's responses correspond to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: Counts neurons co-active on the top-10 examples of one SAE feature (3 at a >0.5 threshold). This measures how a feature is distributed across neurons, not whether any neuron responds to unrelated inputs. It does not bear on V2's prevalence claim.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M layer_2 mid-MLP (after the GeLU)
rows.operation_detail: Counted neurons above a per-neuron activation quantile across the top-10 examples for feature #52.
rows.note: The count indicates breadth of neuron activation for those examples, not whether the inputs are unrelated for any individual neuron.
rows.check: 60 neurons above their 80th quantile measures how widely the feature is spread across neurons, not neuron polysemanticity. It also comes from a single hand-selected feature.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M layer_2 mid-MLP (after the GeLU)
rows.operation_detail: Inspected the neuron weights in feature #52's feature vector, scaled by its maximum activation.
rows.measure: Estimated number of neurons affected by the feature vector
rows.value: Somewhere between 3 and 80 neurons, maybe several hundred depending on interpretation
rows.note: The author presents this as an interpretive estimate; it does not establish that an individual neuron responds to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: The author's interpretive estimate of how many neurons the feature vector touches (3–80, maybe hundreds). It concerns the feature's spread, not neuron polysemanticity.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M layer_2 mid-MLP (after the GeLU), different dictionary described as having learned the identity
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature vectors with neuron activations across the top-50 high-MCS features.

conditions.value: Different dictionary described as learning the identity

rows.measure: Number of neuron activations correlated with each feature
rows.value: The vast majority of features correlate with only 1 neuron activation
rows.note: This is a comparison of feature-to-neuron correspondence, not a measurement of neurons responding to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: Compares the study's own SAE with a second dictionary that learned the identity (a method comparison). It is not a measure of polysemantic neurons.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The post gives an exploratory case and neuron-count estimates, but these do not establish how common unrelated responses are across neurons or layers (R1–R3).
